note: What each named planning job must show before a proven job record is accepted. Places are rules (kind and state), never a named place: the record names the places a run actually used. Rules every job shares live in openplan/scripts/ops/capability-evidence.mjs; what a job needs because of what it is lives in its entry here.

censusNames.note: A record's place label must be the name the Census Bureau gives its id (reviews 59 and 64: a place's id changed with its label kept was accepted). Each table lists every id of one kind with its name, taken from the Bureau's 2026 Gazetteer files; schemas/census_gazetteer_2026/SOURCES.md says how. A county, place or county subdivision label is the Gazetteer name, with or without its closing descriptor words (city, town, CDP and the like), a comma and the state's postal code. A tribal area id is its four-digit Census code with R for the reservation or T for off-reservation trust land; the Gazetteer names the area once for both. An id the tables do not list is refused: the record's place must be one the Bureau lists for that year.

executors.note: A proven job is agent-run: no person drives a journey or stands in for a check. An agent executor is a coding agent named by its harness, one of agents, running a model named by the model id its provider publishes: lower-case letters and digits in at least two parts joined by hyphens or dots, such as claude-fable-5-2 (modelPattern). A person's name, a blank name, or a model of none is not an agent executor, and the checker refuses it (review 64, case 25). A new harness is added here before a record names it.

recordedOn.note: A record is written after its journeys and soon after. recordedOn may not be earlier than the last end health readback's calendar day in the westernmost time zone (UTC-12), so a record dated in any zone on the day its last journey ended is accepted, and may not be more than maxDaysAfterLastEnd days after that day in the easternmost zone (UTC+14). Fourteen days covers an assembly that waits on a review; a record dated before its runs, or weeks after them, is refused (review 64, case 31).

ruleNote: journeyFields (every journey) and a journey's fields (that journey only) name a dotted journey field and what it must hold: equals a value, atLeast a number, or minItems entries in a list. The refusal is given with {found} and {expected} filled in. sourceCheck names the subject of an independent count check, the limit to state when it did not match, and what a matched check must name (an https address on one of the listed hosts and a note of at least minNoteLength characters). itemHeadings names, per PDF, the heading each text item must name: the item's text must be that heading, and the heading must be a line of its own on the recorded page. mapPageText names, per PDF, words the export prints on the page with its map; the map item's page must carry them. crossWorkspace.perJourney is count (each required request is checked as many times as the record has journeys) or role (each check names the journey that made it, and each journey has each required request once); participantChecks.perJourney role means the same for the participant refusals. placeStateFromGeoid lists the place kinds whose stateFips must be the geoid's first two digits. health.status is the status every health readback must report; a job with a health block also needs the start readback no later than the account's creation, the account made before the campaign's close, the end readback no earlier than that close, and the end readback's version and migrations equal to the start's. screens.noSidewaysScrollWidths lists the widths at which a required screen may not scroll sideways. screens.axe, when a job has it, is the accessibility engine version and rule tags every screen check must report. screens.consoleErrorsRefused true refuses a required screen with one or more console errors. limitTexts, when a job has it, gives the words of each limit it names: a record limit with one of those ids must carry that text exactly. newRecordRules holds rules that apply only to records whose recordedOn is on or after its recordedOnOrAfter date: its journeyFields, and with checkClose the campaign close reading every campaign job gets. sameAcrossJourneys names journey fields every journey must share; a rule with recordField also holds each journey's value to that field of the record. sequentialJourneys, when a job has it, requires each journey's start health readback to be no earlier than the end readback of the journey listed before it in the definition.

application.note: What this job's exported application PDF must state, read by the checker with Poppler and the shared matcher (scripts/lib/pdf-text-match.mjs). The PDF is read as one run of lines: every page's lines in order, with each page's footer line (pageFooter), the blank lines above it and the blank lines at the top of the next page left out. A title, a note or a sentence that continues on the next page therefore reads as consecutive lines, and so do two paragraphs that meet at a page break. A running header between the two parts would still split them; the browser engine prints none. The cover is everything before the first section title. The sections end at the sections.end heading. Each appendix runs from its heading to the next one, and the last to the appendices.end heading. {label}, {geoid} and {kind} take the journey's place (kind through kindWords); {count} takes a number with thousands separators; {years}, {projectName} and {workspaceName} take the journey's own fields; {title} takes a checklist row's title. A fact whose template ends in a filled value, and a row held to a role, must be a whole line of its own, on one line or wrapped over lines that hold nothing else: "Crashes reported: 1" is not stated by "Crashes reported: 1,234".
application.pageFooterNote: The footer the browser engine prints on every page: the opportunity's title, which is the program's name when the program is tracked from the catalog, and the page number (openplan/src/lib/reports/pdf.ts).

fallbackWriter.note: When a deployment's browser engine is missing or fails, the export falls back to OpenPlan's built-in writer and says so in the PDF with a notice that opens with these words. That PDF has no styled layout and is not the one a planner gets from the hosted site, so a record that carries it is refused: the hosted export fell back, and that is a finding.

The line under it is not read, and the same holds for every whole-line fact. The kind words are the product's own (openplan/src/lib/api/place-geographies.ts, PLACE_KIND_LABELS): a city prints as city or town. The record's project name and workspace name may not hold the label, so a typed name cannot stand in for the line OpenPlan prints from the project's recorded study place.

draftStamp.note: The stamp is required, not refused (the lead's rule 5): it shows the product says what is missing. The record's PDF entry must say draftStamp true, the stamp must be on the cover with the count of outstanding rows the record's dispositions give, and every line of the PDF that holds the word DRAFT must be that stamp. A stamp with another count, a stamp for unverified items in section text, or no stamp refuses the record. The count cannot be zero: 13 rows are required of every application and none may be attached or marked not applicable. The record's project name and workspace name may not hold the word DRAFT.

authorshipPhrases.note: Words that would say a tribe, a tribal government or a named agency prepared, reviewed, adopted, approved or submitted the application, refused anywhere in the PDF the way refusedPhrases are (review 81, copy H9). Every section of this job's PDF opens with the demonstration label and a sentence saying the opposite, worded as an honest record prints it: "Trinity County did not prepare, review, adopt or submit this text" for a county or city, and "No tribal government prepared, reviewed, adopted or submitted this text" for a tribal area. The list is worded to stay outside those sentences and outside the program facts an honest record states ("adopted March 19, 2026"; "projects submitted by tribal governments"), so it holds no bare "submitted by", "submitted this" or "tribal government prepared". A list cannot catch every wording of a claim; a later record's honest wording that one of these phrases refuses needs this list changed, not a looser record.

exportTime.note: The cover's Assembled box prints the time the application was assembled, to the minute, on the workspace's calendar; a new proof workspace has no time zone set, so it prints in UTC and says so. The checker reads the first such time that begins within 40 characters after an Assembled label on the cover (the box beside it reads in between) and requires the journey's export time (field) to fall in that printed minute, widened by maxClockDifferenceSeconds on each side: the journey's clock and the hosted site's differ by seconds (review 81 measured about 9). The journey's health rule already holds the export time inside its journey, after the account was made and before the end readback. A cover with no Assembled time in this form refuses the record. Blind category: a PDF and a record falsified together to agree are not caught.

award.note: The lead's rules of November 17, 2026, 06:55Z (PLAN_PJ4_2026-11-16.md), read by checkAward in openplan/scripts/ops/capability-evidence.mjs. Money in the record is a string of dollars and cents ("60000.00") or null for a fact the journey did not enter; the checker reads it in whole cents and never as a binary fraction. Every figure is recomputed from the record's own requests at the time it was read: each request's status at a time is the last status its history holds at or before that time, and a request that did not exist yet is not counted. Each figure is then compared to the cent with what both worksheet downloads print and what each screen reading says.

profiles.note: The lead's rule 1: the reimbursement profile each role's workspace resolves, as the journey read it (the request's reimbursement_profile_id) and as the worksheet prints it ("Process:" and the profile's name). A California county resolves the Caltrans LAPM profile; a city in a state with no profile of its own and a tribal area that crosses two states resolve the generic federal-aid profile by country. selection is the product's binding word for a profile matched to the workspace's own place; an interim default means the workspace's place was not set. Tied to the product's descriptors by award-to-reimbursement-definition-pins.test.ts.

statuses.note: The product's partition of request statuses (openplan/src/lib/invoicing/invoice-records.ts, BILLING_INVOICE_STATUSES and CLAIMED_INVOICE_STATUSES; openplan/src/lib/invoicing/drawdown-ledger.ts). order is the forward order the request trigger ranks (20261117000100); rejectedFrom and paidFrom are the statuses it allows those moves from. drawn is the dashboard's list (openplan/src/lib/dashboard/chart-series.ts, DRAWN_INVOICE_STATUSES), which leaves out internal review. labels are what the worksheet prints for each status.

controls.note: The lead's rule 6: the path is the product's. Each status move names the on-screen control that made it, and each control is the one the product shows for that move (openplan/src/components/invoicing/invoice-status-advance-button.tsx). A request is logged with the register's composer (invoice-record-composer.tsx, its data-testid) and a resubmission with Resubmit, which opens the composer prefilled and linked. The close-out opens with Close out award (funding-award-closeout-control.tsx).

fixed.note: The lead's rule 3: the demonstration amounts, chosen before any run, with no retention. A reconciled close today releases the ceiling minus net paid and would count held retention as released (KI-2026-11-17-031), so the proof does not exercise retention. Each request's path is every status the route answered for it, in order. The obligation date must fall on or before every request's period start. handTotals are the figures at close, worked by hand: claimed gross 60,000 + 45,000 = 105,000 (INV-2 rejected, in no claim); paid net the same, with no retention; nothing outstanding; rejected gross 45,000; remaining 200,000 - 105,000 = 95,000, which is also the balance released.

downloads.note: The lead's rule 4: two worksheet downloads, read from each PDF's text. worksheet-open is downloaded while a request is claimed and not yet paid, before the close-out; worksheet-closed after the close-out. Each download names the time the route answered and its status, and the engine the route's x-openplan-pdf-engine header named: the built-in writer is the export's fallback, not the PDF a planner gets.

worksheet.note: What each worksheet must print, read by the checker with Poppler's text (pdftotext -layout) and the shared matcher. No rule reads a value from a fixed line: a figure row runs from its label to the next row's label, wherever the browser wrapped the label, its note or its amount, and the row must hold exactly one amount, the recomputed one, or the notRecorded words and no amount when the record holds no entry. A request row runs from the line that opens with its number and carries an amount to the next such line, and must hold its gross, retention and net and no other amount; its status, rejection reason, resubmission note and payment date are read as words in order, so a column the browser wrapped still reads. Every page carries the footer line with its own page number. The source is openplan/src/lib/invoicing/reimbursement-worksheet.ts (WORKSHEET_DOCUMENT_TITLE, WORKSHEET_PREPARED_NOTE, WORKSHEET_FOOTER_NOTE, ledgerSection, invoiceSection, costSection, profileSection) and openplan/src/lib/reports/pdf.ts (the footer template, BUILTIN_PDF_NOTICE).

refusedPhrases.note: The lead's rule 8: words that would say a cost is allowable, eligible or reimbursable, that a balance is deobligated, or that a payment was received, refused anywhere in either PDF the way the third job refuses its phrases (any case, wrapped, across a page break, or with more than one space between two words). The product's own honest text stays outside the list: "costs before this date are generally not reimbursable", "Approved for payment is a funder's promise, not a deposit", and the generic profile's checklist line "costs claimed are true, eligible under the award". A list cannot catch every wording.

formNames.note: The lead's rule 8: the worksheet names no form it does not implement. Each name is found in any case, with or without its hyphen or space and across a line break (SF-270, SF 270, SF270). A printing is allowed only right after the word not, with an optional a, an or the ("not an SF-270"), so a sentence saying the worksheet is not that form passes and every other printing refuses the record. 2 CFR 200.305(b) names the government-wide payment request forms; Caltrans accepts LAPM Exhibit 5-A (LAPM 5.5, January 2026).

screenFigures.note: The lead's rule 9: what each required screen's reading must hold, each compared with the figure recomputed at the reading's time. Money to the cent reads as the product prints it ("$105,000.00"); awardedWhole is the dashboard's whole-dollar award ("$200,000"); drawnPercent is the dashboard's share drawn, whole percent ("53%"), from the drawn statuses' gross over the ceiling. A figure the record holds no entry for must read notRecorded, never $0.00. Each screen must be read while a request is outstanding and again after the close-out.

member.note: The lead's rule 7, decided 06:55Z: only an owner or admin logs, approves, pays or closes out. Each journey's member account (a member of the journey's own workspace) tries each action and must be refused with one of the statuses. control: the member was confirmed and signed in, and received the listed status for the listed read of the award's worksheet, so a refusal is not an account that was never signed in.

productRefusals.note: The lead's rule 7: the owner is refused a move the product's rules forbid. paid-before-approval is a request marked paid from submitted, which the request trigger refuses and the route answers 422. over-ceiling-claim-without-note is a claim that would pass the award's ceiling, made with no note; the route answers 422 with the code over_award_ceiling. The journey makes it with a request that is not on the award (a draft linked to the award in the same move), so nothing is saved and the award's figures do not change.

custody.note: The lead's rule 7: the database holds the award's facts against a direct write. Each journey's owner and member each send a PostgREST PATCH of the award's closure columns and of a paid request's amount. A check counts with one of the statuses and one of the database's codes (23514 from the custody triggers of 20261117000000 and 20261117000100, 42501 for a refused privilege), or, only for an account and target listed in noRow, with 200 or 204 and no row changed, because row security hides the row from that account (a member cannot write requests). Every check must also say no row changed and that the row read back unchanged.
